prompt: Bug report from a user: "`trailhead summary` shows `time 0h 44m` for a flat 3.74 km walk. By Naismith's rule that is 44.9 minutes, and the README says times are rounded to the nearest minute." Find the cause and fix it.
bash_commands: git ls-files && cat README.md && grep -rn -i "naismith\|minute\|round" --include=*.py . | head -50
cat -n src/trailhead/report.py && cat -n src/trailhead/plan.py && cat -n src/trailhead/pace.py && grep -rn "h \|divmod\|minutes" tests/ | head -30
cat -n tests/test_report.py tests/test_plan.py && python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5; git status --short

cat tests/test_pace.py | head -5 && cat >> tests/test_pace.py <<'EOF'


def test_format_duration_rounds_to_the_nearest_minute():
    assert format_duration(3.74 / 5) == "0h 45m"  # 44.88 minutes
    assert format_duration(0.5) == "0h 30m"
    assert format_duration(5.1) == "5h 06m"
    assert format_duration(0.9999) == "1h 00m"  # 59.99 minutes carries into the hour
EOF
sed -i 's/^from trailhead.pace import leg_hours, naismith_hours, tobler_kmh$/from trailhead.pace import format_duration, leg_hours, naismith_hours, tobler_kmh/' tests/test_pace.py
cat >> tests/test_report.py <<'EOF'


def test_flat_walk_time_is_rounded_not_truncated(make_track):
    # 3.74 km on the flat is 44.88 minutes by Naismith's rule, shown as 45.
    track = make_track((0, 0, 0), (0, 3.74 / 111.19508, 0), name="Flat Walk")
    summary = summarise(track)
    assert summary.hours * 60 == pytest.approx(44.88, abs=0.01)
    assert "  time      0h 45m" in format_summary(summary)
EOF
python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -15; ruff check; mypy 2>&1 | tail -3
python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -15; ruff check; mypy 2>&1 | tail -3
